overview.description: Money is a two-player card game found in several Arab countries including Jordan, Syria, and Egypt. Players hold their cards in a face-down stack and must play the top card at each turn. The game combines elements of fishing games (capturing matching cards) with a unique 'money' system where picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are set aside and used to buy cards when a player runs out.

history.origins: Money is played in several Arab countries. The name refers to the picture cards which serve as currency in the game. It shares mechanics with children's games like Beggar My Neighbour and Snap, but adds the sophisticated buying mechanic.
timeline: Traditional: Played for generations in Jordan, Syria, and Egypt
Modern: Documented and shared through card game collections
Present: Still played in the Middle East and by Arab communities abroad
history.evolution: The game has remained relatively stable, with minor variations in the number of Jokers used and specific buying rules.
history.cultural: A social game played in Middle Eastern cafes and homes. The buying mechanic reflects real-world economic concepts in a simple, accessible format.

setup.players: Two players. The game is normally played with a standard 52-card pack; some variants add two Jokers. Before dealing, all picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are removed. Each player receives two Kings, two Queens, and two Jacks as their starting money, stored face up in a money area or bank. The remaining 40 numeral cards (Aces count as 1s) are shuffled and dealt equally, 20 cards each, as face-down stacks that players must not look at or reorder.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Optional: 2 Jokers can be added. Suits are irrelevant.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, space for 'money area' (bank) and 'floor' (play pile).
setup.dealing: Before dealing, all picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are removed and each player receives 2 Kings, 2 Queens, and 2 Jacks as their starting 'money'. The remaining 40 numeral cards are shuffled and dealt equally (20 each) as face-down stacks.

rules.objective: Collect all the cards (both numeral cards and picture cards/money), leaving the opponent with nothing.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing the top card of their face-down stack to the 'floor' (play pile). The card is thrown face-down then turned face up.
keyRules: Must play top card of stack each turn
Capture by matching the top card number
Picture cards are money to buy more cards
Goal is to collect all cards

strategy.basic: Pay attention to the top card of the play pile. React quickly to matching cards. Manage your money cards wisely - don't use high-value cards to buy small numbers of cards.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played to predict what might come up. Time your buying to get the best value from your money cards. Force your opponent to use their high-value money cards early.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is possible with practice. Optimize your money exchanges to preserve valuable cards. Use the speed factor to your advantage - play quickly when you know a match is unlikely.
tips: Kings are most efficient for buying (5 cards each)
Don't waste a Queen (15 cards) to buy fewer than 15 cards
Watch your opponent's money area to know what they can buy
Capturing large piles can give you many cards at once
Speed is key - practice recognizing matches instantly
